**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 18, 2026
**Re:** Trenex Flight Provisions, LLC: acquisition of Lakeport Skykitchen, Inc. from Dulaix Hospitality Holdings, Inc. (issues review of deal folder)
**Privileged & Confidential / Attorney Work Product**

---

## I. Background and Scope

We represent Trenex Flight Provisions, LLC ("Trenex" or "Buyer"). Trenex bought all of the stock of Lakeport Skykitchen, Inc. (the "Company") from Dulaix Hospitality Holdings, Inc. ("Dulaix" or "Seller") under a Delaware-law Stock Purchase Agreement (the "SPA").

- **Signing:** July 15, 2026.
- **Purchase Price:** **$48,000,000**, made up of **$42,000,000 in cash and a $6,000,000 Seller Note** (SPA §2.1). The price is subject to working capital adjustment under SPA §§2.4–2.5.
- **Seller Note:** $6,000,000 subordinated note, 6% interest. It matures on **August 3, 2027** (Note §§1, 2.1).

**Timing point.** The instruction refers to protecting the client "before the deal closes." The stock purchase itself **closed on August 3, 2026** (SPA §3.1; Note Issue Date). Any fix to the SPA, Note or Key Employee Agreement therefore needs a signed amendment or waiver from the other party. These are SPA §11.3, Note §7.3 (which may also need Senior Lender consent) and KEA §8.5.

The closing that is still ahead is the **Parent Merger**, the acquisition of Trenex Aviation Services Group, Inc. by Osprey Ridge Capital Partners, expected in Q1 2027. That is the hard deadline for Issue 2. It is also the best point of leverage for bundling the other fixes.

**Documents reviewed:**
1. SPA
2. Seller Note
3. Bill of Sale (galley equipment)
4. Key Employee Agreement with Marisol Okafor-Brandt ("KEA")
5. Letter of Intent dated May 18, 2026 ("LOI")
6. Mutual NDA dated April 6, 2026
7. Trenex's October 9, 2026 Dispute Notice letter

I found five issues, set out below roughly in order of urgency. The Bill of Sale and the NDA raised no material issues (Part III).

---

## II. Issues

### Issue 1: The working capital Dispute Notice was sent after the 30-day window closed

**Where:**
- SPA §2.5(b) (Dispute Notice period; "final and binding").
- Trenex's October 9, 2026 letter, opening paragraph and §1.1 (Closing Statement "received on September 2, 2026").

**What the documents say:**
- **The deadline.** SPA §2.5(b) lets Buyer deliver a Dispute Notice "within thirty (30) days after delivery of the Closing Statement." If Buyer does not, "the Closing Statement and Seller's calculation of Closing Net Working Capital shall be final and binding on the parties." Any item not disputed in a *timely* Dispute Notice is also final and binding.
- **The delivery date.** Trenex's own letter says the Closing Statement was received by email on **September 2, 2026**, at finance@trenexflight.com. That is Buyer's notice address under SPA §11.2.
- **Seller's side was on time.** September 2 is exactly 30 days after the August 3 Closing, so Seller met its own §2.5(a) deadline.
- **The arithmetic.** The Dispute Notice deadline was **October 2, 2026**. The letter is dated and was delivered **October 9, 2026**, which is **37 days after delivery** and seven days late.
- **The fallback reading does not help.** Suppose the email arrived after 5:00 p.m. and counts as delivered the next Business Day (September 3) under §11.2. The deadline would then be October 3, and the letter is still late.

**Why it matters to Trenex:**
- Trenex disputes a **$1,150,000** overstatement of Closing Net Working Capital. The four items are:
  - inventory reserve, $410,000;
  - aged and disputed receivables, $385,000;
  - accrued payroll, $230,000;
  - concession fee accrual, $125,000.
- Dulaix can argue that its $5,620,000 Closing Net Working Capital figure became final and binding on October 2. If so:
  - the §2.5(c) negotiation and Independent Accountant process is never triggered;
  - Trenex's adjustment claim is lost;
  - depending on Estimated Net Working Capital, Trenex could even owe a true-up payment to Seller under §2.5(d).
- **Setoff is affected too.** Trenex's letter reserves setoff against the Note. Under Note §3.2(c), a working capital amount is "finally determined" only when it is final under SPA §2.5. If the Closing Statement is final at Seller's number, there is nothing to set off.
- **The letter does not concede the figures.** It disputes them, so Trenex has not accepted the Closing Statement and the point is still live. Dulaix, however, holds a strong procedural defence.
- **Recasting the claim is risky.** Trenex should expect Dulaix to resist any attempt to repackage the same items as indemnity claims under the financial statement or undisclosed liabilities representations (SPA §§4.5, 4.6). Delaware courts have been reluctant to let a buyer use the indemnity regime to relitigate matters that belong in the purchase price adjustment mechanism. The SPA also keeps the two tracks separate (§9.7 carves out "the procedures in Section 2.5" from the exclusive remedy).

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Get a written waiver or extension now.** Ask Dulaix to waive the timeliness defence or extend the §2.5(b) period nunc pro tunc to October 9, 2026, in a writing signed by Dulaix (§11.3 requires a signed written waiver). Packaging this with the Holder consent Trenex needs under Issue 2 may give Dulaix a reason to agree.
2. **Collect the facts on Dulaix's response.** Has Dulaix engaged in §2.5(c) negotiations, accepted the week-of-October-19 meeting, or produced the working papers requested? Conduct of that kind supports waiver or estoppel arguments. Those arguments are weakened, but not necessarily foreclosed, by the §11.3 written-waiver requirement.
3. **Test whether the clock ever started.** Review whether the September 2 Closing Statement complied with §2.5(a). Was it "prepared under the Accounting Principles" and did it include "reasonable supporting detail"? If it did not, Trenex can argue it was not a valid Closing Statement that started the 30-day period.
4. **Preserve the alternatives.** Assess whether any item reflects knowing misstatement, which falls under the §9.7 fraud carve-out. Separately, assert in writing any independent representation breach claims under §§4.5 and 4.6 within the 18-month survival period (§9.1(a), (d)), recognising the double-recovery risk described above.
5. **Fix internal process.** Calendar all remaining contractual deadlines. Confirm internally why the notice was late, as this may be relevant to privilege and to the client relationship.

---

### Issue 2: Closing the Parent Merger will be a Change of Control default under the Seller Note, which the SPA waiver does not cover

**Where:**
- SPA §6.12 (Parent Transaction).
- Seller Note §1 (definition of "Change of Control"), §5.1(g) (Event of Default) and §5.2 (acceleration).
- SPA §11.10 (Order of Precedence).

**What the documents say:**
- **The SPA acknowledgement.** SPA §6.12 records that Trenex's parent, Trenex Aviation Services Group, Inc., has signed a merger agreement with Osprey Ridge Capital Partners, expected to close in Q1 2027. Seller agrees that the Parent Merger and any resulting change in control of Buyer "shall not constitute a breach of **this Agreement**." It also gives Seller no termination or indemnity right "under this Agreement."
- **The Note definition.** Note §1 defines "Change of Control" to include a transaction in which any Person acquires more than 50% of the voting equity "of any Person that directly or indirectly controls Maker." Limb (b) separately covers "a change ... in the Persons who control any Person that directly or indirectly controls Maker." The Parent Merger falls squarely within both limbs.
- **The Note default.** Note §5.1(g) makes it an Event of Default if "Maker consummates a Change of Control without the prior written consent of the Holder."
- **The remedy.** Under §5.2, Holder may then accelerate the full principal and accrued interest by written notice, subject to the Subordination Agreement.

**Why the SPA waiver does not reach the Note:**
- **Its terms are limited.** §6.12 is expressly confined to breaches and rights under "this Agreement," meaning the SPA. It does not mention the Note or give Holder consent.
- **The Note has its own formalities.** Amendments and waivers of the Note need a written instrument signed by Maker and Holder (Note §7.3).
- **The precedence clause does not rescue it.** SPA §11.10 makes the SPA control over Ancillary Agreements only where there is a *conflict*. Here there is none: the SPA is silent on the Note. In any event, the Note expressly "control[s] as to its payment, maturity and subordination terms," and acceleration is a payment and maturity term.
- **No consent exists.** Nothing in the folder records Dulaix's consent as Holder.

**Why it matters to Trenex:**
- The Parent Merger is expected in Q1 2027, well before the August 3, 2027 maturity. On closing, Dulaix could accelerate the entire **$6,000,000** plus interest.
- Interest would run at the 8% Default Rate while the default continues (Note §2.3).
- Trenex could not pay equity distributions while the Event of Default continues (Note §6(c)). This may matter to Osprey Ridge's post-merger plans.
- Trenex would have to give notice of the default within five Business Days (Note §5.3).
- The Note default may cross-default the Senior Credit Agreement. That needs checking, along with whether the senior lenders' own change-of-control provisions are triggered. Note §5.1(f) is also a cross-acceleration trigger in the other direction.
- Even though subordination may limit Holder's ability to collect, the default gives Dulaix significant leverage. It could be used against Trenex in the working capital dispute (Issue 1) and to resist setoff.
- Osprey Ridge's diligence and closing conditions will likely require this to be cleaned up.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Obtain Holder consent before the Parent Merger closes.** This should be Dulaix's prior written consent, as Holder, to the Parent Merger for purposes of Note §5.1(g). Preferably it should take the form of a Note amendment under §7.3 that excludes the Parent Merger from the "Change of Control" definition. It should be signed by Maker and Holder, with Senior Lender consent if the Subordination Agreement requires it.
2. **Fallback: prepay.** Prepay the Note in full before the Parent Merger closes. Note §2.6 allows prepayment without premium, subject to subordination. The cost is that Trenex gives up its setoff security for indemnity and working capital claims.
3. **Align the merger documents.** Review the Parent Merger agreement's covenants and conditions. Make obtaining this consent a pre-closing workstream with Osprey Ridge.
4. **Take nothing from the SPA acknowledgement.** Do not rely on §6.12 for the Note in any communications. Dulaix will hold Trenex to the Note's own terms.

---

### Issue 3: The KEA customer non-solicit covers only the ten largest 2025 airline customers, not all customers as the LOI contemplated

**Where:**
- KEA §5.2 (Non-Solicitation of Customers).
- SPA §1.1 (definition of "Key Customers").
- LOI §6(d).

**What the documents say:**
- **The KEA restriction.** KEA §5.2 bars Ms. Okafor-Brandt, during employment and for 24 months after, from soliciting, inducing away or interfering with "any Key Customer (as defined in the Purchase Agreement)."
- **The borrowed definition.** SPA §1.1 defines "Key Customers" narrowly, for the customer representation in §4.12. It means "the **ten largest airline customers** of the Company, measured by revenue ... for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025."
- **The LOI term.** LOI §6(d) contemplated "a covenant not to solicit **all customers of the Company**."
- **No conflict for the precedence clause to resolve.** SPA §11.10 does not help, because the KEA expressly adopts the SPA definition.

**Why it matters to Trenex:**
- Ms. Okafor-Brandt is the Company's head of operations. Under KEA Recital B and §1.2 she has access to customer relationships, pricing, menu and provisioning specifications and airport arrangements. The LOI calls her continued service "essential to the Transaction."
- As drafted, she may freely solicit, for herself or a competitor:
  - every airline customer outside the 2025 top ten;
  - every customer won after fiscal 2025;
  - any non-airline customer.
- The protected list is also frozen as of 2025, so it will become less relevant over time.
- The goodwill Trenex paid for is therefore only partly protected.
- The LOI's covenant terms were non-binding (LOI §12). They help as evidence of the intended deal but do not by themselves create an enforceable broader covenant.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend KEA §5.2 to replace "Key Customer (as defined in the Purchase Agreement)" with a standalone definition.** The new definition should cover all customers of the Company. For enforceability under Delaware law it can be tailored, for example: "any Person that is, or at any time during the 24 months preceding the date of determination was, a customer of the Company or any of its Affiliates, and any prospective customer to which the Company made a written proposal during that period."
2. **Signatures and consideration.** The amendment must be signed by Ms. Okafor-Brandt and the Company (KEA §8.5). We should offer fresh consideration, such as a modest bonus or an increase to the retention bonus, to support enforceability.
3. **Retain the existing protections.** Keep the §5.6 reformation clause and Buyer's third-party beneficiary right (§7.2) so the expanded covenant has the best chance of being enforced.

---

### Issue 4: Trenex has an uncapped indemnity for Dulaix's credit support, including pre-Closing defaults

**Where:**
- SPA §1.1 (definition of "Seller Credit Support Obligations").
- SPA §9.3(c) (Buyer indemnity).
- SPA §9.5(b) (Buyer cap).
- SPA §6.9 and Schedule 6.9.

**What the documents say:**
- **The Buyer indemnity.** §9.3(c) requires Buyer to indemnify Seller Indemnitees for all Losses "arising out of ... the Seller Credit Support Obligations." This includes any payment made or liability incurred under them.
- **The definition reaches back before Closing.** §1.1 defines Seller Credit Support Obligations as Dulaix's guarantees, letters of credit, surety bonds and other credit support for the Company's airport concession agreements and commissary leases. It also includes "all obligations of Seller ... under that credit support, **whether arising before or after the Closing**."
- **The cap does not apply.** §9.5(b) caps Buyer's liability at **$4,800,000** but provides that "this limitation shall not apply to Losses under Section 9.3(c)."

**Why it matters to Trenex:**
- **No ceiling.** Trenex's exposure for Dulaix's guarantee liability is **uncapped**.
- **Pre-Closing defaults are included.** The exposure extends to defaults from before the August 3, 2026 Closing, when Dulaix owned and ran the Company. Examples are unpaid pre-Closing rent or concession fees, which the Dispute Notice suggests may exist (the $125,000 July concession fee accrual).
- **The risk allocation is asymmetric.** Seller's indemnity to Trenex for pre-Closing matters is subject to a $360,000 basket and a $4,800,000 cap (§9.5(a)). Trenex's indemnity back to Seller for the same period has no limit.
- **Potential circularity.** A pre-Closing breach could support a capped Trenex claim against Dulaix, while Dulaix's guarantee payment on the same breach becomes an uncapped Trenex obligation to Dulaix.
- **Size and duration are open-ended.** The total exposure depends on the concession and commissary obligations in Schedule 6.9, which can be large over multi-year terms. It lasts until Trenex obtains releases under §6.9, which require only commercially reasonable efforts and have no deadline.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend §9.3(c) and the definition.** By SPA amendment under §11.3, limit Buyer's indemnity to obligations arising out of periods *after* the Closing. Expressly exclude Losses from any pre-Closing act, omission or default of the Company or Seller, and any matter for which Seller is obligated to indemnify Buyer under §9.2.
2. **Cap and sunset the indemnity.** Bring §9.3(c) within a cap, either the existing $4,800,000 or a separately negotiated, Schedule 6.9-sized amount. Add a sunset tied to the scheduled expiry of the underlying agreements.
3. **Reduce exposure in the meantime.**
   - Obtain Schedule 6.9 and quantify the guaranteed obligations.
   - Seek estoppel certificates from the airport authorities and landlords confirming no pre-Closing defaults.
   - Accelerate replacement credit support and releases under §6.9.
4. **Negotiate as a package.** Include this amendment in the package with the Note consent (Issue 2).

---

### Issue 5: Tax representations expire August 3, 2027 because survival is tied to the Seller Note maturity

**Where:**
- SPA §9.1(b) (tax representation survival).
- Seller Note §2.1 (Maturity Date).
- SPA §11.10 (Note controls its maturity).
- SPA §§4.14, 9.1(a), 9.1(c), 9.2(c) (related provisions).

**What the documents say:**
- **The survival clause.** SPA §9.1(b) says the §4.14 Tax representations survive "until the **Maturity Date of the Seller Note**."
- **The Note maturity.** Note §2.1 fixes the Maturity Date at "twelve (12) months after the Issue Date (August 3, 2027)." Under SPA §11.10, the Note controls its own maturity terms.
- **The result.** The Tax representations survive only about 12 months, to **August 3, 2027**.
- **Comparison with other survival periods:**
  - General representations survive **18 months** (to February 3, 2028) under §9.1(a).
  - Fundamental Representations survive for the statute of limitations plus 60 days under §9.1(c).

**Why it matters to Trenex:**
- **The reps cover exposure that stays open for years.** §4.14 covers filing and payment for tax years **2023 through 2025**, audits, waivers of limitations and tax sharing agreements.
- **Limitations periods run long.** The federal assessment period is generally three years from filing (IRC §6501(a)) and six years for substantial omissions. There is no limit in cases of fraud or non-filing. State periods are often similar or longer. A 2025 return filed in 2026 can therefore be assessed into 2029 or later.
- **Most exposure will surface too late.** Most pre-Closing tax assessments will arise after Trenex's tax representation claims have expired. That is even earlier than the end of the ordinary 18-month survival period, which inverts the market norm for tax representations.
- **Setoff disappears at the same moment.** Tying survival to maturity means Trenex's claim window and its setoff security end together. Once the Note is paid at maturity, Trenex is left with an unsecured claim against Dulaix.
- **The standalone tax indemnity is also exposed.** §9.2(c) indemnifies pre-Closing Taxes and is not itself a representation. Trenex can argue it survives independently under §9.1(c) ("in accordance with [its] terms"), but the SPA does not say so expressly. Dulaix will likely argue the §9.1(b) cut-off applies to tax claims generally.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Amend §9.1(b).** Provide that the §4.14 representations, and the §9.2(c) pre-Closing Taxes indemnity, survive until **60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations** (including extensions and waivers). This matches the treatment of Fundamental Representations.
2. **Decouple survival from the Note.** Remove the link to the Note Maturity Date entirely, so that any amendment, prepayment or extension of the Note cannot affect tax survival.
3. **Consider extra security.** Seek a tax escrow or holdback, or keep a portion of the Note outstanding, to secure pre-Closing tax exposure after August 3, 2027.
4. **Protect claims under the current terms.** If the amendment is not obtained, calendar August 3, 2027. Have the Company's tax advisors complete a review of 2023–2025 positions before then, so any claims can be asserted in writing with reasonable specificity under §9.1(d) before survival expires.

---

## III. Documents With No Material Issues

- **Bill of Sale (Galley Equipment).** It is consistent with SPA §3.2(a)(iv) and LOI §9. It transfers the equipment free and clear for no additional consideration. Representations are channelled through SPA Article IX, so the same caps, and the same survival points noted above, apply. Recommended housekeeping: confirm Seller delivered the §3.2 records within 10 Business Days.
- **Mutual NDA.** It is between Trenex Aviation Services Group, Inc. and Dulaix and runs to April 6, 2028. SPA §6.3 limited its role for Company information to the period before Closing. Its employee non-solicit (§6) carves out arrangements made with Company employees in connection with the deal with Dulaix's knowledge, so it does not affect the KEA. One point to note: Dulaix's obligations regarding Trenex information, such as integration and financing plans, continue. This may be relevant when sharing Parent Merger details while seeking the Holder consent under Issue 2.

---

## IV. Summary and Priorities

| # | Issue | Location | Exposure | Deadline / Priority | Recommended Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Late Dispute Notice (37 days vs. 30) | SPA §2.5(b); Oct. 9 letter | $1,150,000 working capital claim; Closing Statement may be final and binding | Immediate | Seek Dulaix's written waiver or extension; build arguments challenging finality; preserve alternative claims |
| 2 | Parent Merger triggers Note Change of Control default | SPA §6.12; Note §§1, 5.1(g), 5.2 | Acceleration of $6,000,000 plus Default Rate interest; possible cross-default | Before Parent Merger closes (Q1 2027) | Obtain Holder written consent or Note amendment (plus Senior Lender consent if required), or prepay |
| 3 | Non-solicit limited to ten 2025 Key Customers | KEA §5.2; SPA §1.1; LOI §6(d) | All other customers unprotected | High | Amend KEA to cover all customers, with fresh consideration |
| 4 | Uncapped credit support indemnity, including pre-Closing | SPA §§1.1, 9.3(c), 9.5(b) | Unlimited | High | Limit to post-Closing obligations; cap and sunset; get estoppels and releases |
| 5 | Tax representation survival ends Aug. 3, 2027 | SPA §9.1(b); Note §2.1 | Pre-Closing tax claims cut off | Before Aug. 3, 2027 | Amend to statute of limitations plus 60 days; consider tax escrow; diligence before expiry |

**Overall strategy.** The one thing Dulaix will need to give Trenex before Q1 2027 is Holder consent to the Parent Merger (Issue 2). We recommend approaching Dulaix promptly with a single amendment and waiver package covering:

- the Note consent (Issue 2);
- the timeliness waiver for the Dispute Notice (Issue 1);
- the §9.3(c) and §9.5(b) fix (Issue 4);
- the §9.1(b) survival reset (Issue 5).

The KEA amendment (Issue 3) can proceed in parallel directly with Ms. Okafor-Brandt.

I am happy to prepare the draft amendment package and the waiver request letter to Dulaix.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 18, 2026
**Re:** Trenex Flight Provisions, LLC / Lakeport Skykitchen, Inc.: Issues Review of Transaction Documents

---

## I. Background and Scope

We represent Trenex Flight Provisions, LLC ("Trenex" or "Buyer"). Trenex bought all of the stock of Lakeport Skykitchen, Inc. (the "Company") from Dulaix Hospitality Holdings, Inc. ("Dulaix" or "Seller"). The deal ran under a Delaware-law Stock Purchase Agreement dated July 15, 2026 (the "SPA").

**Purchase price.** Under SPA Section 2.1, the purchase price is **$48,000,000**. It consists of **$42,000,000 in cash** and a **$6,000,000 Seller Note**. Trenex is the Maker of the Seller Note and Dulaix is the Holder.

**Timing.** The SPA's Closing occurred on **August 3, 2026** (SPA Section 3.1). The deal is therefore no longer pre-closing. The exposures below arise in two ways:

- Some arise from post-closing mechanics, such as the working capital adjustment.
- Others turn on the still-pending merger of Trenex's parent, Trenex Aviation Services Group, Inc., with Osprey Ridge Capital Partners (the "Parent Merger"). That merger is expected to close in Q1 2027.

The Parent Merger is now the critical upcoming closing to protect against.

**Documents reviewed:**

1. Stock Purchase Agreement (D1)
2. Subordinated Promissory Note / Seller Note (D2)
3. Bill of Sale – Galley Equipment (D3)
4. Key Employee Agreement – Marisol Okafor-Brandt (D4)
5. Letter of Intent dated May 18, 2026 (D5)
6. Mutual NDA dated April 6, 2026 (D6)
7. Trenex dispute letter to Dulaix dated October 9, 2026 (D7)

Four issues follow, in rough order of urgency. Section VI covers documents that raised no material issues.

---

## II. Issue 1: Working Capital Dispute Notice Delivered After the 30-Day Window

**Where it appears**
- SPA Section 2.5(b)
- Trenex's October 9, 2026 letter (D7), opening paragraph and Section 1.1

**The problem**

SPA Section 2.5(b) gives Buyer **thirty (30) days after delivery of the Closing Statement** to deliver a Dispute Notice. If Buyer does not, "the Closing Statement and Seller's calculation of Closing Net Working Capital shall be **final and binding** on the parties."

Trenex's own letter states two dates:

- The Closing Statement was **received on September 2, 2026**, by email to finance@trenexflight.com. That is the Buyer notice address under SPA Section 11.2.
- The letter itself was **delivered on October 9, 2026**.

The 30-day window therefore closed on **October 2, 2026**. The Dispute Notice went out **37 days** after delivery, which is seven days late. We should confirm the precise time of the September 2 email. Even so, a deemed next-Business-Day delivery under Section 11.2(c) would move the deadline by only a day. It would not cure the lateness.

**Why it matters**

Trenex disputes a **$1,150,000** overstatement of Closing Net Working Capital. The Closing Statement shows $5,620,000; Trenex calculates $4,470,000. The disputed items are:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Obsolete and expired inventory | $410,000 |
| Aged and disputed airline receivables | $385,000 |
| Accrued payroll | $230,000 |
| Concession fee accruals | $125,000 |

Dulaix can take the position that the Closing Statement became final and binding on October 2. If that position holds:

- Trenex loses the Section 2.5(c) negotiation and Independent Accountant process.
- Trenex loses any Section 2.5(d) true-up payment.
- Trenex loses the related setoff right under Seller Note Section 3.1. Under Seller Note Section 3.2(c), a working capital amount is "finally determined" only when Closing Net Working Capital becomes final under SPA Section 2.5. On Dulaix's reading, the final figure is Seller's own figure.

There is a further problem. Under SPA Section 9.7, Section 2.5 is the exclusive post-closing route for working capital items. This makes it hard to bring the same items back as indemnity claims.

The letter shows that Trenex has not accepted the Closing Statement, so the point is live. However, Dulaix has not yet conceded timeliness, and we should assume it will object.

**Recommendation**

1. **Approach Dulaix promptly for a written waiver or extension** of the Section 2.5(b) deadline under SPA Section 11.3. Ideally, obtain this before Dulaix formally asserts finality. This could be offered as part of the negotiation over the Note consent discussed in Issue 2.
2. **Preserve and build alternative arguments.** Possible lines are:
   - whether Seller's email delivery complied with Section 11.2, including the sender, the time of day, and whether it was sent to the designated address;
   - whether the Closing Statement contained the "reasonable supporting detail" Section 2.5(a) requires (if it did not, the 30-day period arguably never started);
   - any course of dealing or communications suggesting extension or waiver;
   - whether any disputed items independently support claims for breach of representations (for example, SPA Sections 4.5 and 4.6) or fraud, both of which fall outside Section 9.7's exclusivity.
3. **Do not set off** any part of the $1,150,000 against Note interest payments until this is resolved. A setoff of an amount that is not "finally determined" risks a payment Event of Default under Seller Note Section 5.1(b).
4. Implement a deadline-tracking protocol for the remaining post-closing notice periods.

---

## III. Issue 2: Parent Merger Will Trigger a Change of Control Event of Default Under the Seller Note

**Where it appears**
- SPA Section 6.12 (Parent Transaction)
- Seller Note Section 1 (definition of "Change of Control"), Section 5.1(g) and Section 5.2
- SPA Section 11.10 (Order of Precedence)

**The problem**

In SPA Section 6.12, Seller acknowledges the Parent Merger. Seller agrees that the merger, and "any resulting change in the ownership or control of Buyer[,] **shall not constitute a breach of this Agreement**." That protection is expressly limited to "this Agreement," meaning the SPA.

The Seller Note is a separate instrument and is treated as such:

- **Seller Note Section 1** defines "Change of Control" to include any transaction in which a Person acquires more than 50% of the voting equity of "any Person that **directly or indirectly controls Maker**." It also covers any change in the Persons who control such a controlling Person. Osprey Ridge's acquisition of Trenex Aviation Services Group, Inc. falls squarely within both limbs.
- **Seller Note Section 5.1(g)** makes it an Event of Default if "Maker consummates a Change of Control **without the prior written consent of the Holder**."
- **Seller Note Section 5.2** allows the Holder, on written notice, to declare the full unpaid principal and accrued interest immediately due. Default interest also accrues at 8% under Sections 2.3 and 1.

Nothing in the folder records Dulaix's consent as Holder. SPA Section 6.12 cannot reasonably be read as that consent:

- It addresses breach, termination and indemnity rights under the SPA only.
- Seller Note Section 7.3 requires any waiver of the Note to be in a written instrument signed by Maker and Holder. It also requires Senior Lender consent where the Subordination Agreement calls for it.
- SPA Section 11.10 provides that the Seller Note controls its own "payment, maturity and subordination terms." Acceleration is a payment and maturity term, which weakens any argument that the SPA overrides the Note.

**Why it matters**

On the Parent Merger closing, expected in Q1 2027, Dulaix could accelerate the full **$6,000,000** principal plus accrued interest. It could also charge default interest and recover collection costs under Section 7.1.

The acceleration would come months before the August 3, 2027 maturity. Several further consequences follow:

- Trenex would lose the benefit of the planned 12-month seller financing.
- It would face a liquidity demand at the moment of its parent's change of ownership.
- It could face cross-default and other complications under the Senior Credit Agreement and the Subordination Agreement.
- It would lose leverage on the Section 9.6 setoff right.
- Section 5.3 independently requires Trenex to notify Dulaix of the default within five Business Days.

The issue also gives Dulaix substantial leverage in any negotiation, including the working capital dispute in Issue 1.

**Recommendation**

1. **Obtain Dulaix's written consent as Holder** to the Parent Merger under Seller Note Section 5.1(g), **before the Parent Merger closes**. A cleaner alternative is a written Note amendment under Section 7.3 carving the Parent Merger out of the "Change of Control" definition.
2. Confirm whether the Senior Lender's consent is required under the Subordination Agreement, and obtain it at the same time.
3. Coordinate with the parent's M&A counsel. The merger agreement's closing conditions and timetable should account for this consent. Funding should also be lined up so the Note can be prepaid at closing without premium under Section 2.6, if consent cannot be obtained on acceptable terms.
4. Consider negotiating the consent together with a resolution of Issue 1.

## IV. Issue 3: Key Employee Non-Solicit Covers Only the Ten Largest Customers

**Where it appears**
- Key Employee Agreement (D4) Section 5.2
- SPA Section 1.1 (definition of "Key Customers") and Section 4.12
- Letter of Intent (D5) Section 6(d)

**The problem**

KEA Section 5.2 prohibits Ms. Okafor-Brandt from soliciting, inducing or interfering with "any **Key Customer (as defined in the Purchase Agreement)**." SPA Section 1.1 defines "Key Customers" as "the **ten largest airline customers** of the Company, measured by revenue recognized by the Company for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025," as listed in Disclosure Schedule Section 4.12.

That definition was built for the customer representation in SPA Section 4.12. Imported into the KEA, it limits the non-solicit to a fixed list of ten carriers.

The LOI contemplated something broader. Section 6(d) called for "a covenant not to solicit **all customers of the Company**" during employment and for 24 months afterwards. Each document reads normally on its own. Together, they produce a covenant much narrower than the deal terms.

SPA Section 11.10 does not help. There is no "conflict" between the SPA and the KEA, because the KEA expressly adopts the SPA definition. The LOI's non-binding Section 6 was superseded by the definitive documents. The KEA reformation clause (Section 5.6) allows a court to narrow an overbroad covenant, not to expand a narrow one.

**Why it matters**

Ms. Okafor-Brandt is the Company's Vice President of Operations. She has direct access to:

- customer relationships and pricing;
- menu and provisioning specifications; and
- airport arrangements.

As drafted, she could leave and solicit every airline customer outside the fiscal 2025 top ten. Those customers include smaller current accounts, carriers won in 2026 or later, and future customers. They also include any former top-ten customer whose ranking has changed.

Two other covenants do not close the gap:

- The confidentiality covenant (KEA Section 6) restricts use of Confidential Information, but it does not bar solicitation as such.
- The Seller non-compete in SPA Section 6.7 binds Dulaix and its Affiliates, not Ms. Okafor-Brandt.

This undermines a core goodwill protection that Trenex paid for. The LOI expressly treated her continued service and covenants as essential.

**Recommendation**

1. **Amend KEA Section 5.2**, by a writing signed by the Company and Ms. Okafor-Brandt under KEA Section 8.5. The amendment should:
   - replace "Key Customer (as defined in the Purchase Agreement)" with a standalone definition covering **all customers of the Company**;
   - include customers served at any time during the 24 months before the solicitation or termination of employment;
   - include actively pursued prospective customers.
2. Provide fresh consideration for the amendment (for example, an increase in the Retention Bonus or a one-time payment) to support enforceability under Delaware law.
3. Keep the scope tied to the Company's airline catering and provisioning business, so the expanded covenant remains reasonable.

## V. Issue 4: Tax Representations Expire With the 12-Month Seller Note

**Where it appears**
- SPA Section 9.1(b)
- Seller Note Section 2.1 (Maturity Date)
- SPA Sections 9.1(a), 4.14 and 11.10

**The problem**

SPA Section 9.1(b) provides that the tax representations in Section 4.14 survive "**until the Maturity Date of the Seller Note**." Seller Note Section 2.1 fixes the Maturity Date at "**twelve (12) months after the Issue Date**," which is **August 3, 2027**. SPA Section 11.10 confirms that the Note controls its own maturity terms.

Read together, these provisions mean the tax representations expire on **August 3, 2027**. That date is:

- **Shorter than the 18-month general survival period** in SPA Section 9.1(a), which runs to February 3, 2028. This inverts the market norm, under which tax representations typically survive *longer* than general representations.
- **Far shorter than the assessment periods** for the Company's 2023–2025 returns. Those are the returns covered by the Section 4.14(a) representation. Federal and state taxing authorities generally have at least three years from filing to assess, and longer in some cases. Audits of 2025 returns may not even begin until well after August 2027.

Linking survival to the Note may have been intended to align claims with the setoff right. In practice, the setoff right also disappears once the Note is paid at maturity.

There is also a related exposure. A prepayment of the Note does not change the defined Maturity Date. However, if the Note is accelerated or restructured (see Issue 2), arguments may arise about when "the Maturity Date" occurs.

**Why it matters**

Pre-closing tax liabilities are among the most likely post-closing exposures in a stock deal, because the Company's tax history comes with the Shares. Trenex would lose any representation-based claim for an audit adjustment, penalty or interest asserted after August 3, 2027.

Trenex would still have the separate pre-closing tax indemnity in SPA Section 9.2(c). Its survival is not expressly addressed. Dulaix will likely argue that it is subject to the same limitation, or that Section 9.1(b) signals the parties' intended time limit for tax matters. Section 9.1(d) preserves claims asserted before expiry, but that is of little use where the assessment arrives later.

**Recommendation**

1. **Amend SPA Section 9.1(b)** by written agreement under SPA Section 11.3. The tax representations in Section 4.14 should survive **until sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations**, including extensions and waivers, consistent with the Fundamental Representations in Section 9.1(c).
2. Confirm expressly that the Section 9.2(c) pre-closing tax indemnity survives for the same period.
3. Consider separate security for tax claims after the Note is repaid, such as a holdback, escrow or guarantee from Dulaix. Otherwise setoff will no longer be available.
4. In the meantime, diligence the Company's 2023–2025 returns. Any known or suspected exposures should be asserted in writing with reasonable specificity before August 3, 2027, to preserve them under Section 9.1(d).
